E1.claim: Supabase's own Edge Function example reads x-forwarded-for and selects element [0].
E1.assessment: Element [0] is the CALLER-CONTROLLED end of an append-style XFF chain. The example is not a provenance contract and, under the observed append behaviour in E3, reading [0] is affirmatively unsafe.

E2.claim: use_remote_address:true / Envoy XFF handling is documented ONLY for the SELF-HOSTED gateway.
E2.quote: use_remote_address: true | Treats Envoy as an edge proxy: uses the peer connection IP as the trusted client address (rather than trusting client-supplied X-Forwarded-For) and strips untrusted x-envoy-* request headers
E2.assessment: Cannot be transplanted onto the hosted platform. Confirms the 2026-09-05 finding F28-A is still open on 2026-09-09.

E3.claim: Community report demonstrates hosted platform APPENDS the real address after a caller-supplied value.
E3.assessment: Corroborates that (a) a caller CAN inject a leading element, and (b) at that time the trustworthy value was the LAST element. Community observation is not a versioned contract; hop count is not guaranteed stable.

E4.claim: Supabase's rate-limiting example does not demonstrate anonymous client identity.
E4.observed: No client-IP extraction shown. Counter backend is Upstash Redis. Keying described only as 'can even rate limit based on the user ID from Supabase Auth'.
E4.assessment: Confirms no first-party anonymous-identity pattern exists. Redis is the example's choice, not a requirement.

trustedInputEvidence.netAssessment: F28-A REMAINS OPEN on 2026-09-09. No authoritative hosted-platform statement establishes the XFF overwrite/append rule, the trusted proxy chain, or hop count. Any design MUST therefore treat the header as structurally untrusted and be safe under an unknown/changing chain.

theoremRestated: Confirmed from 2026-09-05 F28-C and independently re-derived: if a returning client can present exactly the observations of a fresh same-network client, no server can distinguish them. Reset-resistance therefore REQUIRES at least one trusted scarce input. The candidate scarce inputs are: (1) server-observed network address, (2) minting cost (CAPTCHA/proof-of-work), (3) device attestation, (4) anonymous Auth (whose own scarcity is itself (1)).
